headline: Possession and panic in Miami: Colombia's excellence wasted
story: Colombia dictated from the start, pressing high and probing wide through Santiago Arias, but early wastefulness—a gilt-edged chance gone begging in the second minute—set the tone. Portugal, in their compact 4-2-3-1, answered by pressing higher (2.7 phases to Colombia's 2.1), disrupting the hosts' rhythm when it threatened to take flight. The match became a contest between Colombia's possession and Portugal's shape, neither quite resolving it.

Colombia's 1.85 expected goals to Portugal's 0.97 should have won the game. Yet four big chances went begging: a Colombian chance early (2'), another at 62 minutes, and two Portugal openings at 39 and 42 minutes, the first saved. Diogo Costa (8.3 rating) was Portugal's standout; Jhon Arias created tirelessly for Colombia but found no finishing partner. Recovery time mattered: Portugal took 26.3 seconds to the ball, Colombia 17.6, showing defensive discipline buried the visitors' advantage.

keyMoment.text: Colombia's chance in the opening minute, squandered, foreshadowed an evening when neither side could convert their opportunities into goals

home.verdict: Possession and pressure proved insufficient against Portugal's defensive discipline
points: 24 shots with just 7 on target: quantity overwhelmed quality in Colombia's attack
1.85 expected goals created but zero scored—they needed to convert one of their two big chances to win
Press intensity (2.1 high-press phases) was sound; the striker partnership's clinical edge was not

away.verdict: Resilience compensated for limited attacking threat, but only just
points: 0.97 expected goals on 13 shots: low volume, but each chance needed clinical finishing to change the result
2 shots on target is a critical weakness; converting either chance at 39' or 42' wins the match
Diogo Costa (8.3 rating) was essential—the save at 39' was the difference between defeat and a point

statLine: Colombia's 1.85 expected goals and 24 shots could not overcome their own profligacy and Diogo Costa's excellence.
